summary: BBN's host status report for January 31 to February 11, 1972. It lists hosts excluded from daily testing. It was replaced by RFC 315.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 306 reports ARPANET host status from January 31 to February 11, 1972. It lists daily connection test results and identifies hosts that were user-only or not expected to serve regularly.

subtitle: A report of ARPANET host status from January 31 to February 11, 1972.

tldr.problem: Network participants needed status information about hosts that might provide services to other sites.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists daily test results, hosts excluded from testing, and host status or predictions for January 31 through February 11.
tldr.outcome: RFC 306 is an early ARPANET host status report and was obsoleted by RFC 315.

today: RFC 306 is an early host status report and was obsoleted by RFC 315.

sections.title: Hosts Included in the Report
sections.content:
The report covers most Network Hosts from January 31 to February 11. It excludes hosts not expected to function regularly as servers for at least two weeks and hosts intended only as users, including Terminal IMPs and the Network Control Center computer used to gather network statistics.

A table also records each site's server status or prediction, such as Server, User only, or Soon.
sections.plainLanguage: The report focuses on hosts that might serve other network sites. It separately lists hosts that were user-only or not expected to serve regularly.

sections.title: Daily Test Results and Status Codes
sections.content:
The daily table records test results for hosts by site number, site, and date. Its codes are O for Open, D for Dead, H for Half Open, R for Refused, and T for Timed out. A host is timed out if it does not complete the ICP and open a connection within 60 seconds.

The report notes that some sites had announced that their systems might be unavailable at the marked times. It also explains that the BBN Terminal IMP could not test the UCLA IBM-360/91 Network Job Service directly.
sections.plainLanguage: The codes show whether a host opened a connection, was unreachable, refused, or timed out. A timeout means the host did not open within 60 seconds.

sections.title: Availability Notes
sections.content:
The second table records each host's status or prediction and the person providing that information. Examples include a limited server, an experimental server, user-only hosts, and hosts expected to become servers soon.

The report distinguishes test results from these status or prediction statements. It does not claim that every host listed as a server was accessible during every test.
sections.plainLanguage: The status table gives reported roles and expectations, while the daily table shows test results. A server designation does not mean the host passed every test.
